item.title: CrossTalk Bullhorns: No peace
item.description: Vice President J.D. Vance left Islamabad without a deal as the Americans like to put it. It was always unlikely any progress would be made to end the war the US and Israel started. Clearly, this conflict is far from over. Also, NATO has fallen on hard times. We explain why. CrossTalking with Mark Sleboda and George Szamuely.

item.title: Blockade vs blockade
item.description: Trump claims Iran wants a deal “very badly” as the US blockade begins in Hormuz. It is not clear what this blockade aims to achieve other than further global economic dislocation. Trump is not only running out of options, he is running out of time. CrossTalking with Muhannad Ayyash, Esteban Carrillo Lopez, and Ali Alizadeh.

item.title: Decision time
item.description: Starting the US-Israel war on Iran was easy, ending it seems almost impossible. America’s overwhelming military power has proven to be indecisive as Iran holds significant high cards. Eventually the global economy will force Trump’s hand. CrossTalking with Pye Ian and Nadim Houry.

item.title: Ceasefire limbo
item.description: It’s called a ceasefire, but the fighting continues. The US-Israeli war of choice has destabilized the global economy and strengthened Iran. Trump warns that time is running out, and he is right – for his presidency and failed strategy. CrossTalking with Mohammad Marandi, Luciano Zaccara, and Syed Farid Alatas.

item.title: Deadlock
item.description: Has the US-Israel war of choice on Iran become a ‘forever war’ – a war that cannot be won? On this edition of CrossTalk, we examine strategy. Iran has demonstrated that it is methodical and patient. It is unclear if the Trump administration has ever had a coherent strategy. CrossTalking with Raed Jarrar, Seyed Hossein Mousavian, and Michael Scheuer.
